prompt: Our React + TypeScript app re-exports everything through barrel files: every folder has an index.ts that re-exports its contents, and there's a big src/components/index.ts too. Imports look like `import { Button, Modal, Card } from '@/components'`. We now do almost all our editing through Claude Code and Cursor. Is the barrel-file pattern helping or hurting us, and would you keep it?
assertions: Recommends dropping the reflexive per-folder and big aggregator barrels in favour of direct path imports
Grounds it in agent indirection: the barrel hides where a symbol lives, so the agent hops or guesses the shape
Keeps a deliberate barrel only at a real public-API / package boundary (does NOT say delete all barrels)
Names at least one concrete secondary cost (circular imports, tree-shaking, or slow build/test startup)
